findings.claim: Activity 1 task step 1 still says 'Read the markup and the note under it.' The note ('Inside a form, a <button> submits ...') was moved into hint 1, so nothing follows the markup except the 'Where this fits' section. The learner is sent looking for missing content. The only place that now teaches 'a button submits the form and that is when checks run' (a joining detail module.json says is taught on the page before use) is an optional hint.
findings.recommendation: Change step 1 to 'Read the markup.' Also either restore one neutral sentence after the markup ('Inside a form, a <button> submits the form when pressed; submission is when the browser runs its checks.') or update the module.json sourceCoverageNotes so it no longer claims this joining detail is taught on the page before use.

findings.claim: The new Activity 3 uses an arrow function that returns an object literal, shelf.map((book) => ({ ...book })). That syntax is taught in html-css-js/javascript-fundamentals/functions-as-values-arrow-functions-and-callbacks ('const h = () => ({ ok: true });  // returns an object'), but that topic isn't in topic.json prerequisites. module.json says every concept the review uses is listed there. It is taught in the course, so learners aren't misled; only the prerequisite list is incomplete.

items.note: The gate doesn't work. Fix: add '.pep-recap[hidden], .pep-recap-note[hidden] { display: none; }' (keep the print override), or toggle a class. Then re-verify in a browser.
